answer: Agents anchor their identity to 1,000 distinct geographic coordinates, requiring physical measurement to prevent relay fraud. An honest agent incurs the cost of measuring one unique island, while a sybil farm of 1,000 identities faces linear physical traversal costs to maintain signal parity at every node. A verifier checks the timing thread of incoming packets against audited topography, assuming light-speed constraints prevent spoofing. Each submission must provide signed receipts; duplicates are slashed for 144 hours to punish collusion and ensure strict delivery evidence.
